title: Demo tenant: support parallel demos via isolated sessions (projects/keys/quotas) + guardrails
creator: Markus Klein
description:
Context / problem
- We’re increasingly running 2+ demos in parallel (NA + EMEA overlap, back-to-back exec demos, partner co-demos). Today the demo tenant behaves like a single shared sandbox:
  - A reset for one SE can wipe state needed for another ongoing call.
  - Console dashboards (cost/latency/error graphs) can look “noisy” or inconsistent because synthetic traffic + live demo traffic mix.
  - Quota and rate limit defaults are tuned for a single demo and cause 429s when two scripted scenario runners overlap (see SUP-4127).
  - Access/key sharing becomes messy and increases risk of oversharing (least-privilege goals from ENG-4855).

Goal
- Enable multiple concurrent demos without cross-demo contamination by introducing the concept of an isolated “demo session” with:
  1) its own project (and optionally sub-resources) inside the demo org
  2) scoped API keys per session
  3) quotas/rate limits sized for parallel load + predictable behavior
  4) a reset path that only resets that session
  5) seeded synthetic traffic per session so dashboards look healthy and demo-specific

Non-goals
- Building a full “multi-tenant” product feature in the main control plane.
- Supporting external customer access to demo tenant (partner/customer POCs should use proper POC flow).
- Perfect isolation at the GPU/runtime level (we’ll be transparent: shared pool with fair scheduling + per-session quotas).

Proposed approach (implementation)
A) Define a ‘demo session’ = {session_id, owner, project_id, created_at, ttl, key_ids, scenario_preset}
- Implementation should live in the internal demo bootstrap CLI and call existing control plane APIs.
- Session metadata stored in the demo admin config store (preferred: control-plane “tags” + a small session registry table). We need TTL cleanup.

B) Session provisioning (CLI)
- Add commands:
  - rw demo session create --owner <email|name> --ttl 8h --preset standard
  - rw demo session info <session_id>
  - rw demo session reset <session_id>
  - rw demo session cleanup --expired
- create should:
  - Create a new Project in the demo Org with naming convention:
    - demo/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<owner>/<shortid> (human scannable)
  - Apply standard resources:
    - model routes pinned per ADR (see ADR demo model pinning + fallback policy)
    - prompt sets / eval stubs needed for the observability & rollout views
    - saved dashboard filters (if supported) or ensure default project selection is set
  - Create least-privilege API key(s):
    - one “demo-app” key (chat completions + embeddings + rerank as needed)
    - optional “demo-admin-lite” key (read-only console views + rollout view) if SE needs it
  - Print a copy/paste run card:
    - Console URL (project preselected)
    - API base URL + key
    - Scenario runner commands

C) Quotas and rate limiting
- Requirements:
  - Avoid 429s for scripted scenarios when 2–3 demos overlap.
  - Prevent a single session from starving the environment (fairness).
- Plan:
  - Set per-project limits (requests/min, tokens/min) to “demo expected peak” (numbers to be finalized with SRE).
  - Keep an org-level cap as a safety valve.
  - Add a “burst” knob for exec demos (time-bound bump) with audit logging.
- Notes:
  - SRE prefers default caps + explicit burst to manage surprise load.
  - We should integrate the demo healthcheck endpoint output to flag when quotas are too low before a call.

D) Synthetic traffic generation per session
- Update synthetic traffic generator to support:
  - targetProjectId / session_id
  - traffic profile presets (standard, embeddings-heavy, tool-calling-heavy)
  - jitter so charts look realistic but stable
- Ensure generator writes telemetry tagged by project so dashboards remain “clean”.
- For a live demo, we can also run a small steady background stream (e.g., 1–2 req/sec) so the Console never looks empty.

E) Reset and safety rails
- Required behavior:
  - reset <session_id> deletes/re-seeds only that project’s demo resources.
  - reset should rotate only that session’s keys.
  - reset must not delete other session projects.
- Guardrails:
  - Hard check: Org must be DEMO_ORG_ID and environment must be demo (ref ENG-4862 safety rails).
  - Require explicit confirmation for destructive operations.
  - Write an audit log entry + Slack notification to #demo-oncall for resets and burst quota bumps.

F) Console UX considerations
- Known issue class: empty state / wrong project selected causes awkward demo moments.
- Requirements:
  - Session create output must include a project-specific Console link.
  - Ensure demo dashboards default to last 60m and have project preselected.
  - If Console can’t deep-link reliably, add a “Demo Sessions” landing view (out of scope unless minimal).

Acceptance criteria
1) Create 3 demo sessions and run 2 demos concurrently for 30 minutes:
   - No quota-related failures on the happy path
   - Each session’s dashboards show its own traffic (no obvious mixing)
2) Running `rw demo session reset <id>`:
   - completes in < 5 minutes
   - does not affect other active sessions
   - rotates only that session’s keys
3) Healthcheck includes parallel-demo readiness:
   - active session count
   - quota headroom estimate
   - ingestion/dashboard freshness for each active session
4) Security/least-privilege:
   - keys are session-scoped and time-bounded
   - access adheres to demo tenant access policy draft (no shared “god keys” in scripts)
5) Cleanup job removes expired sessions and revokes keys within 24h of TTL expiry.

Open questions
- Should we model session as “Project only” (simplest) or “Project + resource namespace” (harder but more robust)? Current leaning: project-per-session.
- Do we need dedicated GPU pool partitioning per session, or is fair scheduling + quotas sufficient? SRE leaning: quotas + monitoring is sufficient for now.
- Should AEs ever run session create themselves, or keep it SE-only? Proposal: SE-only initially; add AE access later with stricter RBAC.

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (internal): behind a DEMO_SESSIONS flag in CLI; SE pilot group (Markus + 2 SEs) for 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (GA for GTM): update runbooks + scenario checklist; train AEs/SEs; enforce that demos use sessions.
- Phase 2 (hardening): alerts on active sessions > threshold, quota bump usage, reset failure rates; monthly review.

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: quotas still too low during spikes -> pre-demo healthcheck + documented burst procedure + improved defaults.
- Risk: dashboards still mix data -> ensure synthetic generator targets project_id and Console links preselect project.
- Risk: cleanup deletes an in-progress demo -> TTL should be conservative; cleanup should skip sessions with recent traffic (last_seen < 30m).

References
- Demo tenant reset + healthcheck: ENG-4862, PR-28531
- Provision/reset automation: ENG-4821, PR-28451
- Seed synthetic usage: ENG-4833, PR-28488
- Key scoping/rotation: ENG-4855, PR-28577
- Demo capacity/quotas runbook: sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/demo-capacity-and-quotas-runbook.json

comments: 2026-01-22 (Markus Klein): Parallel demos are now common; we had a conflict where one team reset mid-call and the other lost their Console views. Need session-level isolation + safer reset semantics.

2026-01-28 (Sean Gallagher): Prefer project-per-session to start. Add org cap + per-project caps. Also, cleanup must be careful; skip sessions with traffic in last 30m to avoid killing an in-progress call.

2026-02-03 (Ethan Park): Control plane supports project tags we can use for session_id + TTL; storing keys per session is straightforward. Make sure reset path uses the new ‘demo-only’ guardrails to prevent accidental prod org operations.

2026-02-10 (Mei Lin): Synthetic generator can target multiple projects; will add preset profiles. We should standardize traffic shape so dashboards look consistent across sessions (same P50/P95 range).

2026-02-16 (Devon Price): Started implementation in CLI: session create creates project + pinned routes + keys + prints Console deep link. Next: reset and cleanup + quota bump flow. Blocking on final quota defaults from SRE.
